A black hole is the densest kind of object. A red giant is a star that has swollen to a huge size, so its matter is spread out and its density is very low. White dwarfs and neutron stars are very dense, and the Sun is in between.

Sodium and aluminium are in the same period. Moving across a period the nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer, so atoms get smaller. Sodium comes before aluminium, so the sodium atom is larger.
Diamond and graphite are pure forms (allotropes) of carbon, so carbon is free in them. Marble is calcium carbonate and wool is a protein, so in them carbon is combined with other elements.

A metal that reacts with both an acid and a base to give salt and hydrogen (like aluminium or zinc) is amphoteric. It is a metal, so it is electropositive: (i) true, (iv) false. Its oxide is amphoteric, showing both basic and acidic nature, so (ii) and (iii) are true.

reasoning: Both have 8 protons, so both are oxygen, but they have different numbers of neutrons (mass numbers 16 and 18): they are isotopes. Isotopes have the same chemical properties but different physical properties such as mass and density. They are not isobars (different mass numbers) and not different elements.
Vinegar (pH about 3), black coffee (about 5) and urine (about 6) are acidic, with pH below 7. Blood has a pH of about 7.4, slightly basic, so it is the odd one out.

Water is \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), with two hydrogen atoms for each oxygen atom. On electrolysis oxygen collects at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode, and the volume of oxygen is half the volume of hydrogen.

Borax is \(\mathrm{Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O}\): 2 sodium, 4 boron and 7 oxygen atoms with 10 molecules of water of crystallisation. Epsom salt is \(\mathrm{MgSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\) and Glauber's salt is \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4 \cdot 10H_2O}\).

In \(\mathrm{XCl_2}\) the metal combines with two chloride ions, so its valency is 2. The sulphate ion has valency 2, giving \(\mathrm{XSO_4}\), and two hydroxide ions are needed, giving \(\mathrm{X(OH)_2}\).
